Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:1.hebrew: דאיבני אימת - הך חששא דחיישינן למהרה יבנה — אימת תגמור המלאכה, דאיכא למיחש לאיסור חדש כל היום, דאצטריך לרבן יוחנן בן זכאי למיסר השתא כל היום משום סירכא דההוא יומא:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:1.english: When will it be rebuilt? - [As for] this concern that we fear [regarding] “speedily [the Temple] will be rebuilt” — when will the construction be completed, such that there is cause to fear a prohibition of new grain for the entire day, so that Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai needed to forbid [it] now for the entire day because of the habit of that day?

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:2.hebrew: אי נימא דאיבני בשיתסר - שלא נבנה עד יום ט"ז עצמו:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:2.english: If we say that it will be rebuilt on the sixteenth - That it will not be rebuilt until the sixteenth day itself.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:3.hebrew: הרי התיר האיר המזרח - ושפיר קאכלי, דהואיל דהאיר המזרח ואין מקדש בנוי, אשתרי ליה בחדש:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:3.english: Behold, the illuminating of the eastern sky permitted - And they rightfully eat, for since the eastern sky illuminated and the Temple was not built, the new [grain] became permitted to them.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:4.hebrew: אלא דאיבני בחמיסר - או קודם לכן, דכי מטא שיתסר, לא התיר האיר המזרח, שהרי המקדש בנוי. הלכך, אכלי איסורא, וגזר ריב"ז השתא משום ההוא יומא:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:4.english: Rather, that it will be rebuilt on the fifteenth - Or prior to that, so that when the sixteenth arrived, the illuminating of the eastern [sky] did not permit [the new grain], for the Temple was [already] built. Therefore, they [might] eat forbidden [grain], and Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai decreed now on account of that day.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:5.hebrew: מחצות היום ולהלן נשתרי - השתא, דאי נמי אכלי ההוא יומא מחצות היום ולהלן כסירכא דמעיקרא — נכלי, וליכא איסורא, דודאי קרב העומר:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:5.english: From midday and onward let it be permitted - Now [in our time]; for even if they eat on that day from midday and onward according to their previous habit, let them eat, and there is no prohibition, for the omer has certainly been offered.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:6.english: As we learned [in a mishna] - In tractate Menachot (ibid.).

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:7.hebrew: הרחוקים - מירושלים, לא היו רואין ולא היו שומעין שעת הקרבת העומר:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:7.english: Those who are distant - [Distant] from Jerusalem, [who] would neither see nor hear the time of the offering of the omer.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:8.english: Are permitted - With [regard to] new grain.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:9.hebrew: מחצות היום ולהלן - לפי שיודעים שאין ב"ד מתעצלים בו מלהקריבו קודם חצות:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:10:9.english: From midday and onward - Because they know that the court is not indolent regarding it [so as to delay] offering it before midday.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:11:1.hebrew: לא צריכא דאיבני בליליא - כלומר, לשמא יבנה בליליא חייש, ולא יהו פנויים לקצור העומר עד סמוך ליום. ויש טורח הרבה בעומר, שהיו מייבשין אותו באבוס של קלאים, וצוברין אותו שיזובו מימיו, וטוחנין אותו ברחים של גרוסות, ומניפין אותו בי"ג נפה, בגסה בדקה, כדאמרינן התם. וזה, שלא יוכלו להתעסק בו מתחילת לילה, לא יספיקו להקריבו למחר קודם חצות:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:11:1.english: No, it is necessary [where] it was rebuilt at night - That is to say, [the Tanna] is concerned lest it be rebuilt at night, and they will not be free to harvest the omer until close to daytime. And there is much labor involved in the omer, for they would dry it in a roasters' trough, and heap it up so that its moisture would drain, and grind it in a groats mill, and sift it through thirteen sieves, [ranging from] coarse to fine, as we say over there; and [due to] this, that they will not be able to engage in [preparing] it from the beginning of the night, they will not manage to sacrifice it tomorrow before midday.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:11:2.hebrew: אי נמי - דאיבני בחמיסר סמוך לשקיעת החמה, והיא היא. ואי קשיא: דבלילה אינו נבנה — דקי"ל בשבועות (דף טו:) דאין בנין בית המקדש בלילה, דכתיב: "וביום הקים", ולא בחמיסר שהוא י"ט — דקי"ל בשבועות (שם) דאין בנין ב"ה דוחה י"ט? ה"מ בנין הבנוי בידי אדם, אבל מקדש העתיד שאנו מצפין, בנוי ומשוכלל הוא, יגלה ויבא משמים, שנא' (שמות ט״ו:י״ז): "מקדש ה' כוננו ידיך":
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:11:2.english: Alternatively - That it was rebuilt on the fifteenth [of Nisan] close to sunset, and it is the same [rationale as when rebuilt at night]. And if [you raise] a difficulty: It cannot be built at night, as we hold in Shevuot (15b) that the building of the Temple is not [done] at night, as it is written: "And on the day that [the tabernacle] was erected" [Numbers 9:15]; nor [can it be built] on the fifteenth, which is a Festival, as we hold in Shevuot (ibid.) that the building of the Temple does not override a Festival? This applies only to a building constructed by human hands; but the future Temple for which we yearn is [already] built and perfected; it will be revealed and come down from heaven, as it is stated (Exodus 15:17): "The Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established."

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:11:3.hebrew: בשיטת ר' יהודה - אותה שיטה שהיה ר' יהודה, שהיה מתלמידי תלמידיו, דורש אחריו — דרש גם הוא בימיו:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:11:3.english: In accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda - That [same] opinion that Rabbi Yehuda, who was among the disciples of his disciples, expounded after him — he [Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai] also expounded in his [own] days.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:1:1.hebrew: בזכרים - שאין מגדלים מהם וולדות, ואפ"ה גזרו רבנן אטו נקבות:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:1:1.english: With regard to males - For one does not raise offspring from them, and even so, the Sages decreed [a prohibition] on account of females:

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:2:1.english: Rav Ashi said: [This] dispute - [That] of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yochanan.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:2:2.hebrew: בפרי ראשון - בפירות שביעית הוא דא"ר אלעזר דרך חילול לא, משום דדריש סמוכין:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:2:2.english: With regard to original produce - It is with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year that Rabbi Elazar said that by means of redemption it is not effective, because he expounds juxtaposed verses.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:2:3.english: Secondary produce - The proceeds of Sabbatical-Year produce.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:2:4.english: And that which is taught - In the baraita that supports him [Rabbi Elazar].

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:2:5.hebrew: לקח לקח - בכולהו, בין בפרי ראשון בין בדמיו, דקתני ״לקח בבשר יין״, ולא קתני ״חילל בשר ביין״:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:2:5.english: “Purchased, purchased” - In all of them, both with the original produce and with its proceeds, as it teaches: “He purchased wine with meat,” and does not teach: “He deconsecrated meat with wine.”

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:2:6.english: Since the first clause taught "purchased" - For it deals with the produce itself.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:3:1.hebrew: וביקש לו ליקח חלוק - ואינו יכול, דהתורה אמרה: "לאכלה" — בתוך הזמן, ולא לסחורה, וזה מתקיים לשנה הבאה:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:3:1.english: And he sought to purchase a garment for himself - And he cannot [do so directly], for the Torah said: “For food” — within the [designated] time, and not for commerce; and this [garment] lasts into the following year.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:3:2.english: Who is accustomed to him - For because of this, he will fulfill his wish.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:3:3.english: And then he says to him - To the storekeeper.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:3:4.hebrew: הרי פירות הללו - שמכרת לי, שהיו של חולין ונכנסו לקדושת שביעית, נתונים לך במתנה, ואוכל אותם בשביעית. והחנוני אומר לו: ואני נותן לך סלע חולין זה, שיצא לחולין, במתנה. ובא ולוקח מאותו סלע כל מה שירצה, והחנווני יאכל הפירות בתורת שביעית:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:3:4.english: These fruits - “[These fruits] that you sold me, which were non-sacred and entered the sanctity of the Sabbatical Year, are given to you as a gift, and eat them in [accordance with the laws of] the Sabbatical Year.” And the storekeeper says to him: “And I give you this non-sacred *sela*, which has been deconsecrated, as a gift.” And [the customer] goes and purchases whatever he wants with that *sela*, and the storekeeper eats the produce under the law of the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:3:5.hebrew: והא הכא - דהא סלע פרי שני הוא, דמי שביעית, וקתני דצריך לילך אצל חנווני ולהוציאו לחולין דרך מקח וממכר. אלמא, בפרי שני נמי איכא מאן דפליג. דאי הוי סגי בדרך חילול — למה ילך אצל חנווני? יקח פירות חולין שיש לו בביתו שוה סלע, ויחללנו עליהם, ויאכלם בתורת שביעית:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:3:5.english: But here - For this sela is secondary produce, [namely,] money of the Sabbatical Year, and [the baraita] teaches that he must go to a storekeeper and deconsecrate it by way of purchase and sale. Evidently, regarding secondary produce there is also someone who disputes [it]; for if it were sufficient by way of redemption, why should he go to a storekeeper? Let him take unconsecrated produce that he has in his house worth a sela, redeem [the coin] upon them, and eat them under the laws of the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:4:1.hebrew: אלא - אי אתמר דרב אשי, הכי אתמר:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:4:1.english: Rather - If [the statement] of Rav Ashi was stated, it was stated as follows:

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:4:2.hebrew: מחלוקת בפרי שני - בהא הוא דאיכא למאן דשרי דרך חילול, אבל פרי ראשון כו':
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:4:2.english: The dispute is with regard to secondary produce - It is in this [case] that there is one who permits [it] by way of redemption; but [regarding] original produce, etc.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:4:3.hebrew: והא דקתני - בברייתא דמסייע לר' יוחנן: "אחת שביעית ואחת מעשרות מתחללין" — אלמא שביעית עצמה דרך חילול:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:4:3.english: And that which is taught - In the baraita that supported Rabbi Yoḥanan: "Both Sabbatical-Year [produce] and tithes are deconsecrated" — implying that Sabbatical-Year [produce] itself [is deconsecrated] by way of redemption.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:5:1.hebrew: מעשר מעשר ממש - בתמיה: וכי יש לומר שהמעשר עצמו יתחלל על בהמה, חיה ועוף:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:5:1.english: "Tithe" — actual tithe produce? - [This is said] in astonishment: Could one say that the [second] tithe itself could be deconsecrated upon cattle, undomesticated animals, or fowl?

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:5:2.hebrew: והכתיב - "ונתתה בכסף וצרת", דאין מתחלל אלא על המטבע — דבר שיש עליו צורה:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:5:2.english: And isn’t it written - “Then shall you turn it into money, and bind up [the money]” — for [second tithe] is deconsecrated only upon a coin, an item that has a minted form upon it.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:6:1.hebrew: במקדש שבעה - כדדרשינן בת"כ מושמחתם לפני ה' אלהיכם שבעת ימים (ויקרא כ״ג:מ׳) — ולא בגבולין ז' ימים:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:6:1.english: In the Temple [for] seven [days] - As we expound in Torat Kohanim from "And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days" (Leviticus 23:40) — and not in the provinces seven days.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:6:2.english: In the province - [Even] in Jerusalem, for it too is like the provinces.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:7:1.hebrew: ושיהא יום הנף - של עומר, דהיינו ט"ז בניסן, כולו אסור בחדש. ובעוד המקדש קיים, משקרב העומר היו אוכלין חדש בו ביום, כדכתיב (שם): "עד הביאכם". וכשחרב הבית, מותר מן התורה משהאיר המזרח, כדאמר במנחות (דף סח.): כתוב אחד אומר: "עד עצם היום הזה", דהיינו האיר המזרח; וכתוב אחד אומר: "עד הביאכם". הא כיצד? בזמן דאיכא עומר — "עד הביאכם", ובזמן דליכא עומר — "עד עצם". ואסר רבן יוחנן בן זכאי עליהם כל היום, כדמפרש טעמא בגמרא:
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:7:1.english: And that the day of waving - Of the omer, that is, the sixteenth of Nisan, [should be] entirely prohibited for [eating] new grain. And while the Temple stood, once the omer was offered, they would eat new grain on that very day, as it is written (ibid.): “Until you bring [the offering of your God].” And when the Temple was destroyed, it was permitted by Torah law once the eastern horizon illuminated [at dawn], as it says in Menachot (68a): One verse says: “Until this very day,” which means [once] the eastern horizon illuminated; and one verse says: “Until you bring [the offering of your God].” How is this [reconciled]? When there is an omer [offering] — “Until you bring”; and when there is no omer [offering] — “Until the very [day].” And Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai prohibited [it to] them for the entire day, as [the Gemara] explains the reason in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sukkah 41a:9:1.hebrew: מהרה יבנה בית המקדש - ויחזור דבר לאיסורו, דהשתא קרינא ביה "עד הביאכם". ואי הוו נהיגי בחורבנו לאכול בהאיר מזרח כדין תורה, אתיא למיכל נמי בבניינו, ויאמרו: אשתקד מי לא אכלנו, כו':
Rashi on Sukkah 41a:9:1.english: Soon the Temple will be rebuilt - And the matter will return to its prohibition, for now [that there is a Temple] we read regarding it [the verse]: "Until you bring [the offering of your God]." And if they were accustomed during its destruction to eat [new grain] upon the illumination of the eastern [horizon] in accordance with Torah law, they will come to eat [it] also upon its rebuilding, and they will say: "Last year, did we not eat...", etc.

Tosafot on Sukkah 41a:11:1.hebrew: אי נמי סמוך לשקיעת החמה דחמיסר - שלא יוכלו להתעסק בעומר בתחילת לילה, ולא יספיקו להקריב קודם חצות למחר. וי"מ דמיירי בערב י"ט סמוך לשקיעת החמה, ולא יכול לבקר בי"ט מהיכן יקצרו את העומר, והיכן מגלות וקופות ושלש עשרה נפה וכלי שרת — דברים הצריכין לעומר, כדתנן במנחות פ' ר' ישמעאל (מנחות דף סו.). דאי סמוך לשקיעת החמה דחמיסר קאמר, שהוא י"ט — הא אין בנין בית המקדש דוחה י"ט, כדאיתא פרק שני דשבועות (דף טו:)! ולאו פירכא היא, דתיקשי לן: הא דקאמרינן "לא צריכא דאיבני בליליא" — הא נמי אמרינן התם דאין בנין בהמ"ק בלילה, שנאמר: "וביום הקים את המשכן", ביום מקימין אותו ובלילה אין מקימין אותו! אלא על כרחיך צריך לחלק, כמו שפירש בקונטרס: דהני מילי בנין הבנוי בידי אדם, אבל מקדש העתיד — בנוי ומשוכלל יגלה ויבא מן השמים, שנא': "מקדש ה' כוננו ידיך":
Tosafot on Sukkah 41a:11:1.english: "Alternatively, adjacent to sunset" of the fifteenth - [This means that it was built just before sunset at the end of the fifteenth,] so that they will not be able to engage in [preparing] the omer at the beginning of the night, and they will not have enough time to sacrifice [it] before midday tomorrow. And some explain that it is dealing with the eve of Yom Tov [the fourteenth], adjacent to sunset, and one could not inspect on Yom Tov from where they will reap the omer, and where the sickles and baskets and thirteen sieves and service vessels [are] — things that are needed for the omer, as we learned in the Mishnah in Menachot, in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Yishmael" (Menachot 66a). For if it means adjacent to sunset of the fifteenth, which is Yom Tov — behold, the building of the Temple does not override Yom Tov, as is stated in the second chapter of Shevuot (15b)! Yet this is not a [valid] refutation, for let us also raise a difficulty: That which we say, "No, it is necessary [only where] it was built at night" — behold, we also say there that there is no building of the Temple at night, as it is stated: "And on the day that the Tabernacle was erected" (Numbers 9:15) — by day they erect it, but at night they do not erect it! Rather, perforce one must distinguish, as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi]: This applies only to a building built by human hands, but the future Temple will be revealed and arrive from Heaven built and perfected, as it is stated: "The sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands established" (Exodus 15:17).

Tosafot on Sukkah 41a:3:1.hebrew: פירות הללו נתונים לך במתנה - בהדיא קתני בירושלמי דשביעית בסוף פרק שמיני: "והחנווני אומר לו: הרי סלע נתון לך במתנה", ובענין אחר לא סגי. ודייק: דדרך חילול אינו — מדלא חילל החנווני לכתחילה סלע של בעל הבית על פירותיו, שלא כדרך מקח וממכר:
Tosafot on Sukkah 41a:3:1.english: "These fruits are given to you as a gift" - It is explicitly taught in the Yerushalmi of Shevi'it, at the end of the eighth chapter: "And the storekeeper says to him: Behold, [this] sela is given to you as a gift," and in no other manner does it suffice. And [Ravina] deduces that by way of redemption it is not [permitted], from the fact that the storekeeper did not at the outset redeem the householder's sela onto his produce, not by way of purchase and sale.

Tosafot on Sukkah 41a:7:1.hebrew: ושיהא יום הנף כולו אסור - הרבה תקנות תיקן רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, אלא הנך תרתי תיקן יחד, להכי תני הכא יום הנף אגב גררא. ותימה, דבמנחות פרק רבי ישמעאל (מנחות דף סח.) לא תני הנך דלולב אגב ההוא דיום הנף; ובפרק בתרא דר"ה (דף ל.) תניא הנך תרתי ועוד תקנות טובא דתקון:
Tosafot on Sukkah 41a:7:1.english: "And that the entire day of waving should be prohibited" - Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted many ordinances; however, these two he instituted together, which is why [the Mishnah] teaches [the ordinance of] the day of waving here incidentally. And it is astonishing: for in Menaḥot, in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Yishmael" (Menaḥot 68a), it does not teach those [ordinances] of the lulav along with that of the day of waving; and in the last chapter of Rosh Hashanah (30a), these two are taught along with many other ordinances that they instituted!

Tosafot on Sukkah 41a:9:1.hebrew: דאשתקד לא הוה בית המקדש האיר המזרח הוה מתיר - ואפילו לרבי יהושע, דאמר: "שמעתי שמקריבין אף על פי שאין בית" בפ"ק דמגילה (דף י.) — הני מילי כשיש מזבח בנוי, אבל בלא מזבח לא; כדמוכח בזבחים, פרק קדשי קדשים (זבחים דף ס. ושם), דמזבח שנפגם — כל הקדשים שנשחטו שם פסולים, ואין אוכלים בגינו שירי מנחה, ולא קדשי קדשים, ואפילו קדשים קלים:
Tosafot on Sukkah 41a:9:1.english: "That last year, when there was no Temple, the illuminating of the eastern [sky] would permit [it]" - And even according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who said, "I heard that one may sacrifice even though there is no Temple" in the first chapter of Megillah (10a) — this applies only when there is a built altar, but without an altar, no; as is proven in Zevachim, chapter Kodshei Kodashim (Zevachim 60a and there), that [in the case of] an altar that was damaged, all the sacrificial offerings slaughtered there are invalid, and one does not eat the remainder of a meal-offering, nor most-holy offerings, and not even lesser holy offerings on its account.
